title: Solutions to Problems at Les Houches Summer School on EFT
extended_summary:
This paper is a compiled set of worked solutions to exercises from the Les Houches Summer School session on Effective Field Theory (EFT) in particle physics and cosmology. It does not study an educational intervention or compare instructional approaches; instead, it presents theoretical problem solutions covering renormalization, power counting, symmetry transformations, Fierz identities, operator classification, decay calculations, and EFT matching.

The document is organized around lecture-based topics from the summer school, including the renormalization group, EFT basics, operator bases, dimensional analysis, and matching between full theories and EFTs. The material is technical and aimed at readers with graduate-level training in quantum field theory and particle physics. The paper also references the associated lectures and provides derivations for each exercise.

Because the paper is not an empirical study in an educational setting, there is no participant population, no classroom implementation, and no intervention outcome measurement. Its main contribution is as a pedagogical/theoretical companion to the EFT summer school, supplying explicit solutions and derivations for advanced physics exercises.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a physics summer-school solutions document, not an educational intervention study. It contains worked solutions and theoretical derivations, with no K-12 setting, no comparison group, and no empirical evaluation design.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational technology or AI intervention evaluated, and no learner, teacher, or institutional outcome is measured. As a result, it provides no evidence of impact for the requested K-12 research topic.
